title: Investigation of thermal exposure in traditional neyshabur bakeries using heat strain and physiological indices
author: Bolghanabadi, Ganjali, et al.
materials: This cross-sectional study was conducted on 103 workers of the Bakeries in winter 2018. Samples were selected from people who were without cardiovascular disease, respiratory, infectious diseases, and diabetes and hyperthyroid, people who used cardiovascular drugs, beta blockers, diuretics, antihistamines, were not excluded. Before the study, the consent of all persons to participate in this research was drawn and the workers were assured that the information will remain confidential. The questionnaire containing demographic information including age, height, weight, work experience, education, smoking was completed. The normal body temperature was measured by a mercury thermometer. Heart rate was measured using radial pulse counting. Heat stress in the industry was evaluated for each workstation, for each of the individuals was enrolled in the study. To measure WBGT was used Casella model of digital WBGT. Also the HSSI questionnaire was used to assess the validity and reliability of heat strain that reviewed and approved by Dehghan et al. [11], The questionnaire contains 18 questions where variable temperatures, humidity, air movement, intense sweating, intense thirst, fatigue, sadness, clinical signs, levels temperature, ventilation, type of work wear, work wear color, type of protective equipment, workload, body position, dimensions of work space and location of doing tasks has been studied that score obtained from this questionnaire will be considered as an indicator of heat strain. The first 12 questions were asked of respondents, while the last 5 questions were completed after observation of the workers, scores for each item were multiplied by the effective coefficient of each question. Finally, the scores of the items were summed to yield total score. This index has three levels of risk with numbers less than 13.5 (without strain), numbers between 13.6–18 (containing strain) and numbers over 18.1 (certainly containing strain).

steps.title: Define participant eligibility
steps.instruction: Select 103 bakery workers from Neyshabur during winter 2018 who have no cardiovascular disease, respiratory disease, infectious disease, diabetes, or hyperthyroidism and who are not using cardiovascular drugs, beta‑blockers, diuretics, or antihistamines.

steps.title: Obtain informed consent
steps.instruction: Provide each selected worker with an information sheet, obtain written consent to participate, and assure confidentiality of all data.

steps.title: Collect demographic data
steps.instruction: Administer a questionnaire to record age, height, weight, work experience, education level, and smoking status for each participant.

steps.title: Measure baseline body temperature
steps.instruction: Measure each participant’s normal body temperature using a mercury thermometer.

steps.title: Record resting heart rate
steps.instruction: Determine heart rate by counting the radial pulse for each participant.

steps.title: Measure workplace WBGT
steps.instruction: At each workstation, measure the Wet‑Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) using a Casella model digital WBGT meter.

steps.title: Administer HSSI questionnaire
steps.instruction: Use the Heat Strain and Stress Index (HSSI) questionnaire (18 items). Ask the first 12 questions directly to the respondent; observe and record responses for the last 5 questions.

steps.title: Calculate HSSI score and classify risk
steps.instruction: Multiply each item’s response by its effective coefficient, sum all items to obtain a total score, and classify risk: <13.5 = no strain; 13.6–18 = strain; >18.1 = certain strain.

steps.title: Analyze data with SPSS
steps.instruction: Enter all collected data into SPSS software version 24, compute descriptive statistics (mean, standard deviation, range), and assess relationships using t‑test and chi‑square as appropriate.
